full_text_en:
Cheng Kejie Bribery Case

Promulgation No. 33 (2000)

Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China

Criminal Order

(2000) Xing Fu Zi No. 214

The defendant, Cheng Kejie, male, born November 13, 1933, Zhuang ethnicity, native of Shanglin County, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, university education, formerly Vice Chairman of the Standing Committee of the Ninth National People's Congress, formerly Deputy Secretary of the CPC Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Committee and Chairman of the People's Government of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, residing at No. 128 Qixing Road, Qixing Road Area, CPC Committee Compound, Xincheng District, Nanning City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. Arrested on April 25, 2000. Currently in custody.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, having tried the case where the Beijing No. 1 Branch of the People's Procuratorate charged the defendant Cheng Kejie with the crime of bribery, rendered a criminal judgment on July 31, 2000, pursuant to (2000) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 1484, finding the defendant Cheng Kejie guilty of bribery, sentencing him to death, depriving him of political rights for life, and confiscating all his personal property. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Cheng Kejie refused to accept it and appealed. The Beijing High People's Court, on August 22, 2000, rendered a criminal order pursuant to (2000) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 434, dismissing the appeal, affirming the original judgment, and reported the case to this Court for approval in accordance with the law. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, conducted a review of the case, and comprehensively examined whether the facts found in the first-instance judgment and the second-instance order were clear, whether the evidence was reliable and sufficient; whether the applicable law was correct; whether the defendant's criminal conduct, its consequences, and the degree of harm, and whether there existed any statutory or discretionary circumstances for a lighter, mitigated, or heavier punishment; whether a death sentence with immediate execution was absolutely necessary; and whether the trial procedures at both the first and second instances were lawful. After deliberation by the collegial panel, the matter was discussed and decided at the 1128th meeting of the Adjudication Committee. The review is now concluded.

Facts Found Upon Review:

The defendant, Cheng Kejie, and his mistress, Li Ping (a Hong Kong resident, dealt with in a separate case), discussed in late 1993 about divorcing their respective spouses to marry each other, and agreed to first earn money then marry, utilizing Cheng Kejie's official position to seek benefits for others and accept property from others in preparation for their post-marriage life. From early 1994 to late 1997, Cheng Kejie learned from Li Ping that if he assisted the Guangxi Yinxing Industrial Development Company (hereinafter "Yinxing Company") in contracting the Nanning Jiangnan Parking and Shopping Mall project and the Guangxi Minzu Gong project, and in resolving construction funding, he could receive "kickbacks." He then accepted the entreaties of Zhou Kun, the head of Yinxing Company, and using his official powers: placed Yinxing Company under the management of the General Office of the Autonomous Region People's Government; assigned the Nanning Jiangnan Parking and Shopping Mall project to Yinxing Company for construction and requested the Autonomous Region Planning Commission to approve the project as soon as possible; instructed the Nanning Municipal Government to transfer 85 mu of land for the project to Yinxing Company at a low price; assigned the Guangxi Minzu Gong project to be jointly developed and constructed by Yinxing Company and the Autonomous Region Ethnic Affairs Commission, changing the project legal person from the originally designated Ethnic Affairs Commission to Yinxing Company; repeatedly requested the Guangxi Branch of the China Construction Bank and the Guangxi Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China to grant loans totaling RMB 100 million to Yinxing Company; instructed the Autonomous Region Housing Reform Office to illegally lend RMB 25 million in housing reform funds to Yinxing Company; twice instructed the Autonomous Region Department of Finance to lend RMB 50 million in fiscal revolving funds to Yinxing Company; and applied to the State Planning Commission on behalf of Yinxing Company for project subsidy funds of RMB 13 million. In return, Li Ping, on behalf of the parties, accepted bribes from Yinxing Company totaling RMB 29,211,597 and HKD 8.04 million, of which RMB 11.5 million was paid to Hong Kong businessman Zhang Jinghai for converting and withdrawing the bribe money, and informed Cheng Kejie of the receipt of the bribes. During this period, Cheng Kejie also, in collusion with Li Ping, accepted from Zhou Kun bribes in the form of RMB, HKD, USD, gold diamond rings, gold ingots, craft gold lions, Rolex watches, and other items, totaling RMB 559,428, of which items and cash handled directly by Cheng Kejie amounted to over RMB 455,000, all of which were handed over to Li Ping for safekeeping.

From July to October 1994, Cheng Kejie learned from Li Ping that if he helped the Guangxi Trust and Investment Company and its subsidiary, the Guangxi Guixin Industrial Development Company, obtain loans, he could receive "kickbacks." He then accepted the entreaties of these two companies, and using his official position, requested the Guangxi Branch of the China Construction Bank and the Guangxi Branch of the Bank of China to grant loans totaling RMB 16 million to these two companies respectively. The loans were all used by the Guangxi Guixin Industrial Development Company. In return, Li Ping, on behalf of the parties, accepted bribes from the Guangxi Guixin Industrial Development Company totaling RMB 600,000 on two occasions and informed Cheng Kejie of the receipt of the bribes.

In July 1997, Cheng Kejie learned from Li Ping that the Tunnel Engineering Bureau of the Ministry of Railways, through the introduction of Liu Xinmin, Chairman of the Board of Guangxi Guilong Economic and Trade Co., Ltd., was seeking to contract the Laping Tunnel Project for draining the reservoir area of the Yantan Hydropower Station. If he helped the Tunnel Engineering Bureau secure this project, he could receive "kickbacks." He then accepted the entreaties, and using his official powers, instructed the Autonomous Region Resettlement Office to assign the project to the Tunnel Engineering Bureau for construction. Upon learning that the project had already been awarded through bidding, he directly intervened in the bidding process, illegally altering the bidding outcome, resulting in the Tunnel Engineering Bureau, which should have contracted the lower-bid upstream section project, being awarded the higher-bid downstream section project. In return, Li Ping, on behalf of the parties, accepted bribes of RMB 1.8 million from the Tunnel Engineering Bureau through Liu Xinmin and informed Cheng Kejie of the receipt of the bribes.

From early 1994 to April 1997, Cheng Kejie, through Li Ping, accepted the entreaties of Gan Weiren, and using his official powers, facilitated Gan Weiren's successive promotions from Deputy County Mayor of Hepu County, Guangxi, to District Mayor of Tieshangang District, Beihai City, Guangxi, and then to Deputy Secretary-General of the Autonomous Region People's Government. In return, Li Ping, on behalf of the parties, accepted bribes of RMB 270,000 from Gan Weiren on four occasions and informed Cheng Kejie of the receipt of the bribes. Additionally, from early 1996 to February 1997, Cheng Kejie also accepted the entreaties of Zhou Yisheng, former Director of the Haicheng Branch of the Beihai Public Security Bureau, and Li Yihong, former Director of the Service Center of the Autonomous Region Planning Commission. Using his official powers, he recommended Zhou Yisheng to relevant departments for the position of Director of the Beihai Public Security Bureau and facilitated Li Yihong's promotion to Deputy Director of the Autonomous Region Government's Office in Beijing. In return, Cheng Kejie accepted bribes of USD 3,000 from Zhou Yisheng and RMB 18,000 from Li Yihong. The USD 3,000 was handed over to Li Ping for safekeeping.

In total, Cheng Kejie, either alone or in collusion with Li Ping, accepted bribes in cash and items amounting to RMB 41,090,373 in total. After the case was uncovered, all the proceeds were recovered.

Evidence Confirming the Above Facts:

The above facts found in the first-instance judgment and the second-instance order are confirmed by witness testimony, physical evidence, documentary evidence, expert conclusions, and other evidence that was read out, presented, examined, and verified during the first-instance trial. The defendant, Cheng Kejie, has also previously confessed. This evidence has been listed item by item in the first-instance judgment and is reliable and sufficient to establish the facts. This Court hereby affirms it in accordance with the law.

Opinion of This Court:

The defendant, Cheng Kejie, during his tenure as Deputy Secretary of the CPC Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Committee and Chairman of the People's Government of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, utilized his official position to seek benefits for others, illegally accepting property from others either alone or in collusion with Li Ping. His conduct violated Article 385, Paragraph 1, of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and constitutes the crime of bribery. Cheng Kejie and Li Ping conspired to accumulate wealth for their post-marriage life. Li Ping acted as the intermediary to contact the petitioners and collect the bribes, while Cheng Kejie used his official position to seek benefits for the petitioners in matters such as contracting projects, securing funds, and obtaining promotions. Subjectively, Cheng Kejie had the intent to jointly accept bribes with Li Ping; objectively, he engaged in conduct of using his official position to seek benefits for the petitioners and jointly accepting bribes with Li Ping. Therefore, Cheng Kejie's conduct satisfies both the subjective and objective elements of the joint commission of the crime of bribery. The bribes jointly accepted by Cheng Kejie and Li Ping were kept by Li Ping, with the majority being handled and received by Li Ping. This was the division of labor in their joint bribery offense. The fact that these bribes were not directly handled or kept by Cheng Kejie does not affect the determination of Cheng Kejie's bribery crime. As a high-ranking leading official, Cheng Kejie utilized his official position to engage in power-for-money deals, accepting enormous bribes, the amount of which is exceptionally large. His conduct seriously infringed upon the integrity of public officials' official conduct, severely damaged the reputation of public officials, seriously disrupted the normal work order of state organs, and caused extremely adverse social impact. The circumstances of his crime are particularly serious, and he should be punished according to law. Although Cheng Kejie expressed his willingness to return the bribery proceeds, the recovery of the proceeds in this case was achieved with Li Ping's cooperation. Cheng Kejie's expression of willingness to return the proceeds did not play any substantive role in their recovery. Moreover, the recovery of the proceeds cannot remedy the enormous losses caused to the state by Cheng Kejie's bribery conduct and the extremely adverse social impact resulting therefrom. Cheng Kejie does not have any statutory circumstances for a lighter or mitigated punishment. The facts found in the first-instance judgment and the second-instance order are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, the conviction is accurate, and the sentencing is appropriate. The trial procedures at both the first and second instances were lawful. Pursuant to Article 199 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 285, Paragraph (1), of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ordered as follows:

The criminal order of the Beijing High People's Court, (2000) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 434, upholding the first-instance judgment sentencing the defendant Cheng Kejie to death for the crime of bribery, depriving him of political rights for life, and confiscating all his personal property, is hereby approved.

This order shall take effect immediately upon service.

Presiding Judge: Liu Jiachen
Judge: Ren Weihua
Judge: Gao Guijun
September 7, 2000
Clerk: Han Jinping

Editor's Note: The Cheng Kejie bribery case was accepted by the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court pursuant to the Supreme People's Court's designation of jurisdiction. After a public trial, the first-instance judgment was rendered on July 31, 2000.

Cheng Kejie refused to accept the first-instance judgment and appealed to the Beijing High People's Court. The main grounds of Cheng Kejie's appeal and his defense counsel's arguments included: the first-instance judgment's finding that Cheng Kejie and Li Ping prepared money for their marriage and jointly accepted bribes lacked evidence and was not established in fact; holding Cheng Kejie criminally responsible for the joint bribery regarding property that was solely received and possessed by Li Ping lacked legal basis; since specialized banks and local governments do not have a relationship of leadership and subordination, Cheng Kejie's request to relevant specialized banks to issue loans to Yinxing Company, Trust Company, and Guixin Company did not constitute using his official position to seek benefits for others; Cheng Kejie handed over the property given by Zhou Kun to Li Ping for the purpose of returning it to Zhou Kun and lacked the intent to accept bribes; and Cheng Kejie wrote to Li Ping to actively cooperate with relevant authorities in recovering all the property involved in the case, which constituted voluntary surrender, and the first-instance sentence was too severe. The Beijing High People's Court, after the second-instance hearing, found that the grounds of appeal and defense arguments were untenable, decided not to accept them, and rendered the second-instance order dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

The Supreme People's Court has published the first-instance judgment and the second-instance order of this case as appendices to the death penalty approval order on the internet. Due to space limitations, this journal cannot simultaneously publish the first-instance judgment and the second-instance order. Interested readers may consult them on the internet.
